concepts.title: Describe one thing in the present
concepts.explanation: In these singular third-person present descriptions, Hungarian leaves out the English is: A hang természetes. Before a noun, the adjective describes it: egy természetes hang. After the subject it states the quality. Keep this narrow: it is not a rule for every person, tense, existence or location. Day 1 introduced this; read the examples again if it is unfamiliar.

concepts.title: Put nem before the description
concepts.explanation: To negate today’s adjective description, place nem directly before the adjective: A hang nem természetes. There is still no separate is.

concepts.title: An action verb stays
concepts.explanation: An action sentence needs its action verb. A modell segít = The model helps. A telefon küld = The phone sends (context may supply what). Unlike English, these Hungarian present forms can also mean is helping / is sending. Do not add van before segít or küld in these sentences. We practice only these third-person forms.

concepts.title: Mark what someone sends
concepts.explanation: New teaching today, even if it appears later in the planned course: Hungarian often marks the direct object with -t. Learn just two complete pairs: videó → videót; adat → adatot. Ask what is being sent. In Anna egy videót küld, Anna is the sender and videót is what she sends. In A telefon adatot küld, telefon is the sender and adatot is what it sends. The connecting o in adatot is part of this taught form; do not invent a general rule that every noun takes -ot. The indefinite verb form küld fits egy videót and unspecified adatot. A definite object would require a different verb form, which is not tested today.

transliteration.description: A practical pronunciation aid, not a formal transliteration standard. Egyptian pronunciation varies between speakers. The spellings here are consistent within this lesson; small vowel variations are acceptable.
rules: Short a, e, i, o, u are approximate vowels. Double aa, ee, oo mark a longer vowel: hold it a little longer.
sh is like sh in ship. kh is the rough sound in Scottish loch. gh is its voiced counterpart; neither is an English g.
g represents the usual Egyptian pronunciation of the Arabic letter jeem, as in English go.
ʿ marks the Arabic ayin, a voiced throat sound with no exact English equivalent. Try a gentle throat constriction; do not let it stop you speaking.
ʾ marks a glottal stop, the catch between the two parts of uh-oh. It commonly represents qaaf in these Egyptian words, but not every Egyptian word with qaaf is pronounced this way.
h is a beginner approximation for both Arabic h sounds in this lesson. It does not mean that the two Arabic consonants are identical.
el- means the. It sometimes blends into the following consonant: esh-, et-, and en-. These spellings show the spoken sound.
The small word fee means in. In a connected phrase it can join the following article, as fel- or fesh-.

Brand and product names are the one deliberate exception: their familiar official Latin spellings are retained in the pronunciation line. Digits remain digits. They are names to recognize, not new Arabic spelling targets.

conceptRegistry.title: Describe one thing in the present
conceptRegistry.explanation: In these singular third-person present descriptions, Hungarian leaves out the English is: A hang természetes. Before a noun, the adjective describes it: egy természetes hang. After the subject it states the quality. Keep this narrow: it is not a rule for every person, tense, existence or location. Day 1 introduced this; read the examples again if it is unfamiliar.

conceptRegistry.title: Put nem before the description
conceptRegistry.explanation: To negate today’s adjective description, place nem directly before the adjective: A hang nem természetes. There is still no separate is. We are describing an imagined classroom voice, not contradicting a company’s reported claim.

conceptRegistry.title: An action verb stays
conceptRegistry.explanation: An action sentence needs its action verb. A modell segít = The model helps. A telefon küld = The phone sends (context may supply what). Unlike English, these Hungarian present forms can also mean is helping / is sending. Do not add van before segít or küld in these sentences. We practice only these third-person forms.

conceptRegistry.title: Mark what someone sends
conceptRegistry.explanation: New teaching today, even if it appears later in the planned course: Hungarian often marks the direct object with -t. Learn just two complete pairs: videó → videót; adat → adatot. Ask what is being sent. In Anna egy videót küld, Anna is the sender and videót is what she sends. In A telefon adatot küld, telefon is the sender and adatot is what it sends. The connecting o in adatot is part of this taught form; do not invent a general rule that every noun takes -ot. The indefinite verb form küld fits egy videót and unspecified adatot. A definite object would require a different verb form, which is not tested today.

conceptRegistry.title: Keep dates, claims and examples separate
conceptRegistry.explanation: The lesson date is October 4. The privacy source was published October 2, and the Vids source September 29, then highlighted in an October 2 recap. A company’s description such as more natural is attributed to that company. Encrypted data can leave a phone; encrypted does not mean never uploaded or perfectly private. Fictional practice names and descriptions below are not company news.

conceptRegistry.title: Join the parts: no separate is
conceptRegistry.explanation: In these simple present-time identity and adjective sentences, put the parts together without an English-style is. This pattern does not remove action words such as helps or sends.
conceptRegistry.scaffold: 1. Read da as this. 2. Add video. 3. Read the joined line naturally as This is a video. In the last example, helps is an action and remains in Arabic.
conceptRegistry.guidedCheck: Complete the supplied cue: da ___. Use video.
conceptRegistry.scope: Only present identity and adjective descriptions. No full tense or verb system.

conceptRegistry.title: Pair this and new with the noun
conceptRegistry.explanation: Use da with the masculine nouns video, voice, phone and model. Use dee with the feminine noun company. In this small pair, gedeed becomes gedeeda with company. Learn these two complete frames.
conceptRegistry.scaffold: 1. Point to a phone: da mobaayl. 2. Add gedeed after it. 3. Switch to company using the whole feminine frame dee sherka gedeeda. Do not change only one end.
conceptRegistry.guidedCheck: Say the supplied company frame once, then cover it and try again.
conceptRegistry.scope: The three focus examples use basic singular nouns. Data is a supplied non-human plural chunk; do not extrapolate a plural rule today.

conceptRegistry.title: Put mesh before a description
conceptRegistry.explanation: To make today’s adjective description negative, put mesh before its adjective. You can also put it before a noun in a simple identity sentence. This is not a general rule for negating action verbs.
